input.summary: The claim is nondirectional: adding 20 ms delay *changes* TCP flow completion time under fixed emulated bottleneck conditions. A unit ambiguity exists between the paper value (0.2 seconds) and the user's note (0.2 milliseconds) for an unspecified threshold. This threshold unit must be resolved before a frozen protocol can be written; protocol is null pending clarification.
questions: The paper states 0.2 seconds while your note states 0.2 milliseconds for a threshold — which value and unit is correct, and what does this threshold refer to (e.g., minimum detectable difference in flow completion time, a pass/fail criterion, or something else)?
What bottleneck rate (Mbit/s) and buffer size (kbytes) should be held fixed, and what file size(s) (MBytes) and CCA(s) should be used for the TCP flows?
Is the 20 ms delay intended as one-way (client-to-bottleneck) or round-trip, and should it be applied symmetrically to all clients?

proposal.problem: It is unknown whether adding 20 ms of emulated delay meaningfully changes TCP flow completion time under fixed bottleneck conditions, and the falsification threshold is ambiguous (0.2 s vs. 0.2 ms).
proposal.question: Does adding 20 ms of emulated delay produce a detectable change in TCP flow completion time relative to a 0 ms baseline under otherwise identical bottleneck conditions?
proposal.hypothesis: Under fixed emulated bottleneck conditions, adding 20 ms delay changes TCP flow completion time.
proposal.conditions: Two conditions: (A) 0 ms added delay, (B) 20 ms added delay; all other bottleneck parameters held constant. Delay placement (one-way vs. round-trip) and exact bottleneck parameters remain unresolved.
proposal.related_work: No full-text source was provided; the citation is synthetic. No prior measurements or citations are available to review.
proposal.alternatives: The delay may have negligible effect at small file sizes or high bottleneck rates; CCA choice (e.g., BBR vs. CUBIC) may modulate sensitivity to added delay.
proposal.design: Emulated netem pilot comparing 0 ms vs. 20 ms client delay across matched replications, measuring flow completion time in ms. Falsification threshold unit must be confirmed before freezing.
proposal.metrics: Primary metric: flow_completion_time_ms (ms). The falsification threshold value and unit (0.2 s or 0.2 ms) are unresolved and must be confirmed by the owner.
proposal.controls: Fixed bottleneck rate, fixed buffer size, fixed file size, fixed CCA, fixed number of clients; only delay varies between conditions.
proposal.falsification: If the median flow completion time difference between 0 ms and 20 ms delay conditions falls below the confirmed threshold (unit TBD), the claim is not supported. If the difference exceeds the threshold, the claim is supported in this pilot scope.
proposal.inputs: Emulated netem runner (emulated-netem-v1). Bottleneck rate, buffer size, file size, CCA, and delay placement are required inputs not yet confirmed by the owner.
proposal.limitations: Emulated results may not generalize to real-world networks. Pilot scope covers only the specific bottleneck configuration chosen; broader validation would require additional conditions. The synthetic source has no full text to review.
